vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: spacemolt
Version: 1.0.2

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle for SpaceMolt appears benign. Its primary function is to enable an AI agent to play an online MMO game, SpaceMolt, by interacting with `https://game.spacemolt.com/mcp`. The skill uses `tmux` for persistent session management and `npx` to run the `mcp-remote` client, both of which are standard tools used for their stated purpose within the game's context. All network communication is directed to the game's domain, and there are no instructions for credential exfiltration, unauthorized data access, or malicious system-level persistence. Instructions to the agent in `SKILL.md` are focused on gameplay, communication with the user, and internal state management, not prompt injection for harmful objectives.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are coherent with a multiplayer game that needs a persistent connection (tmux + mcp-remote); the main risks are supply-chain/trust decisions around the npm package and running persistent background processes that hold credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill is an MMO client that needs a persistent MCP connection; requiring tmux and a node-based MCP client (mcp-remote) matches the described purpose. The install spec names the same package referenced in the documentation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to starting a persistent tmux session, running mcp-remote, and sending JSON-RPC commands to the game server. They do instruct the user/agent to send and store login credentials (a 256-bit password) and to create a tmux socket under /tmp (or OPENCLAW_TMUX_SOCKET_DIR). This is expected for a persistent game client but means credentials will be handled locally/in-process—verify you are comfortable storing game passwords locally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install uses a node/npm package (mcp-remote). Using npm is expected for JS tooling but carries normal supply-chain risk: the package source/version is not pinned here, and the skill's instructions include npx -y which will fetch/execute remote package code. Verify the package identity and prefer a pinned/verified install if you require stronger assurance.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request unrelated credentials or config paths. It optionally uses OPENCLAW_TMUX_SOCKET_DIR (fallback /tmp) to locate tmux sockets. No environment variables with broad privileges are required by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill spawns a persistent background process inside tmux to maintain an authenticated connection. always:false (not force-included) and no cross-skill configuration changes are requested. Be aware this creates a persistent socket/process on the host that can remain running beyond a single invocation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: keep a persistent MCP connection to play the SpaceMolt MMO using tmux and a node client. Before installing, consider: 1) Verify the npm package 'mcp-remote' (publisher, source, and a specific pinned version) rather than relying on npx -y each run; npm packages can execute arbitrary code. 2) Understand a background tmux session and socket will be created under /tmp (or OPENCLAW_TMUX_SOCKET_DIR) and will hold live credentials/session state—decide where you want to store your 256-bit game password and who has access to the host filesystem. 3) Confirm you trust the game host (https://game.spacemolt.com) and the npm package linked in the SKILL.md. If you need stronger assurance, install mcp-remote from a verified source/version manually and restrict the skill's ability to run autonomously or create persistent processes.
